title: CEO Interview with Pratap Ranade of Arena Physica
gist: Arena Physica CEO Pratap Ranade pitches 'electromagnetic superintelligence': Heaviside-1, a 350M-parameter EM foundation model trained on 250,000 3D field simulations that predicts full-wave field responses ~100,000x faster than solvers within a decibel of commercial accuracy, plus the Atlas agentic harness used by AMD since 2023. The thesis is that simulation, not ingenuity, bottlenecks hardware design, and that proprietary simulated/measured data plus forward-deployed engineers form a moat versus EDA incumbents and generic AI tools.

insights.claim: Arena Physica argues that simulation, not human ingenuity or design, is the bottleneck in hardware verification, since full-wave solver runs take hours or even days each.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: If AI surrogates break the simulation bottleneck, hardware design cycle times and EDA/simulation economics could shift materially.
insights.quote: Simulation is the bottleneck, not human ingenuity or design.

insights.claim: Heaviside-1, released in September, is a 350-million-parameter model trained on 250,000 3D field simulations that predicts the full 3D field response of a structure in milliseconds, roughly 100,000x faster than a traditional solver and within a decibel of commercial accuracy.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A 100,000x speedup claim at near-commercial accuracy is a potential disruption vector for incumbent EM simulation vendors.
insights.quote: That is roughly 100,000x faster than a traditional solver, and within a decibel of commercial accuracy.

insights.claim: Heaviside is trained on electromagnetic fields rather than text as its primitive, positioned as the world's first foundation model for electromagnetics.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Domain-native foundation models (non-text) are an emerging category distinct from LLM providers.
insights.quote: trained on electromagnetic fields over text as a primitive
insights.locator: We execute our mission on two fronts

insights.claim: Heaviside has reached fully autonomous design of 2.5D RF structures: given a target response such as a 7 GHz bandpass filter, the model generates a working geometry, and the company is scaling it from RF toward photonics.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Generative inverse design extending to photonics could address co-packaged optics and other AI-infrastructure hardware.
insights.quote: You specify a target response, such as a 7 GHz bandpass filter, and our model will generate a working geometry.

insights.claim: Arena Physica built its own data factory because the data an EM foundation model needs does not exist publicly: experts seed designs, simulation scales them, and the best candidates are fabricated and measured in its own lab.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Proprietary synthetic-plus-measured data is the claimed moat in physics AI, implying high barriers for generic AI entrants.
insights.quote: A foundation model for EM needs data that doesn’t exist publicly, so we built it ourselves.

insights.claim: AMD has used Arena Physica's Atlas agentic harness since 2023 for Radeon GPU testing and optimization, running tests and tuning jobs autonomously.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Evidence that a major GPU vendor is already using autonomous AI agents in post-silicon validation.
insights.quote: Since 2023, AMD has used Atlas for Radeon GPU testing and optimization, running tests, and tuning jobs autonomously.

insights.claim: In one semiconductor deployment, Atlas ran over a weekend against a farm of newly returned silicon and found a performance-per-watt result beyond what the prior team had reached by hand.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Autonomous post-silicon tuning could extract extra perf/watt from existing chips, a key AI-datacenter metric.
insights.quote: Atlas ran over a weekend against a farm of newly returned silicon finding a performance-per-watt result beyond what the prior team had reached by hand

insights.claim: Arena Physica says it has helped partners cut root-cause analysis time from six hours to thirty minutes and generatively design new specs in ten minutes versus 23 hours manually.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Order-of-magnitude engineering time savings claims support the case for AI-driven hardware productivity.
insights.quote: cut root-cause analysis time from six hours to thirty minutes, generatively design new specs in ten minutes (versus 23 hours manually)
insights.locator: We’re also actively deployed in aerospace

insights.claim: Atlas builds a deterministic graph across electrical, mechanical, software and firmware domains and integrates with tools such as KiCad, Altium, LTSpice and HFSS to orchestrate schematic/PCB design, simulation, EM/SI/thermal analysis, mechanical design and lab instruments in one loop.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Orchestration layers sitting atop incumbent EDA tools may capture workflow value without displacing them.

insights.claim: Heaviside is targeted at EM verification for structures chip teams design today, including BGA packaging, SerDes interconnects, signal integrity, and RF and millimeter-wave circuits.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Advanced packaging and high-speed interconnect verification are high-value AI-infrastructure bottlenecks.

insights.claim: Semiconductor teams on Microsoft Discovery can use Heaviside, giving Arena Physica a distribution channel through Microsoft.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Hyperscaler platform distribution may accelerate adoption of specialized physics AI models.
insights.quote: Semiconductor teams on Microsoft Discovery can use Heaviside
insights.locator: Most enterprise engagements start with one

insights.claim: Arena Physica says AI-infrastructure and defense build-outs are placing extraordinary demands on hardware teams that were already at their limit.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: AI capex and defense spending create derived demand for hardware-engineering productivity tools.
insights.quote: The build-outs in AI infrastructure and defense put extraordinary demands on hardware teams that were already at their limit.

insights.claim: Experienced electrical and RF engineers are scarce because, for roughly the past decade, most technical graduates went into software.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Structural EE/RF talent shortage supports pricing power for tools that automate scarce hardware expertise.
insights.quote: For the past decade or so, most technical graduates went into software; experienced EE and RF engineers are scarce

insights.claim: Hardware customers cannot 'move fast and break things' or 'vibe-code' hardware, and they worry about sensitive IP flowing to a handful of concentrated model providers and paying for tokens without clear return.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Trust, IP concentration and token-ROI concerns may limit general-purpose LLM penetration in hardware engineering, favoring specialized vendors.

insights.claim: Arena Physica launched HW-Bench, which it calls the first hardware engineering benchmark, with founding partners AMD and Anduril, testing whether AI models can complete real engineering jobs end to end and scoring accuracy, cost and speed.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Benchmarks that set evaluation standards can shape vendor selection in AI-for-hardware.
insights.quote: Software had its AI moment; now it’s hardware’s turn.

insights.claim: Arena Physica explicitly does not aim to replace EDA, simulation and test-equipment incumbents; its platform works with their tools and Heaviside hands off to a full-fidelity solver for final sign-off.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Near-term AI surrogates complement rather than cannibalize sign-off solver revenue, though they may compress exploratory simulation demand.
insights.quote: Heaviside is designed to hand off to a full-fidelity solver when a design needs final sign-off
insights.locator: The incumbents in EDA, simulation and test

insights.claim: Arena Physica claims owning the model, platform and application lets deployment learnings feed straight back into research, creating a self-reinforcing feedback loop.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Vertical integration is pitched as the moat against horizontal AI tool vendors.

insights.claim: Arena Physica's go-to-market relies on forward-deployed engineers embedded in customer organizations, starting with an acute problem, a short 'Protoshop' build on real customer data, then pilot and production.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Palantir-style forward-deployed model implies high-touch, services-heavy early revenue.
insights.locator: Most enterprise engagements start with one

insights.claim: Beyond semiconductors, Arena Physica is deployed in aerospace and defense, including phased arrays and radar, and in medical devices, with customers including AMD and Anduril.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Defense exposure (radar, phased arrays) diversifies the end market alongside semiconductors.
insights.locator: We’re also actively deployed in aerospace
